news.title: World Cup could return to UK after 69 years with huge decision today
news.lede: A UK-hosted World Cup could be just hours away from becoming a reality. The 2035 Women’s World Cup is expected to be awarded today, on Monday, November 23 to England, Northern Ireland, Scotland, and Wales. The decision will be made at a special FIFA virtual congress. If successful, it will be the first time the UK has hosted a World Cup since 1966, when England famously lifted the men’s trophy.

news.title: GFA congratulate Black Challenge on historic World Cup triumph, thanks stakeholders for unwavering support
news.lede: The Ghana Football Association (GFA) extends its heartfelt congratulations to the Black Challenge following their historic triumph at the 2026 WAFF Amputee Football World Cup in Mexico, where they overcame Morocco to lift the coveted global trophy. This remarkable achievement has etched Ghana’s name in the history books as only the second African nation to win the prestigious competition, marking another proud moment for Ghanaian football and the nation as a whole. The Black Challenge’s triumph is a shining testament to the team’s courage, resilience, determination and unwavering belief. It also underscores the power of perseverance and the ability to overcome challenges in pursuit of excellence.

news.title: Women's World Cup play-offs: Scotland v Sweden - Andreatta's preview
news.lede: Scotland women play Sweden in Paisley next Tuesday, with the second leg in Stockholm on 5 December. Scotland intend to bring fancied Sweden's World Cup dream "crashing down - and do it in a truly Scottish way", according to women's head coach Melissa Andreatta. Scotland face a two-legged World Cup qualifying play-off against powerhouses Sweden, who are managed by Andreatta's former boss Tony Gustavsson. The Swedes, who have been semi-finalists at the two previous Women's World Cups and are ranked eighth in the world, will be strong favourites to reach the tournament in Brazil next summer.

news.title: Republic of Ireland football: Chloe Mustaki to miss World Cup play-off against Poland with knee injury
news.lede: Chloe Mustaki is a key figure for Carla Ward's Republic of Ireland side. Republic of Ireland defender Chloe Mustaki has been forced to withdraw from her side's 2027 Women's World Cup play-off final against Poland next month after rupturing her anterior cruciate ligament (ACL). The 31-year-old sustained the injury in action for Nottingham Forest against Liverpool in the League Cup last week. Her club have confirmed the centre-back will miss the rest of the season and that their medical team will "determine the best course of action for her rehabilitation and recovery".

news.title: Amputee World Cup: Ghana win first title, beat Morocco 1-0
news.lede: Ghana won the Amputee World Cup for the first time on Sunday night, beating Morocco 1-0 in San Juan de los Lagos, Mexico, with a goal from captain Richard Opentil in the 32nd minute. The win makes Ghana’s Black Challenge the second African side to be crowned world champions in amputee football, after Angola in 2018, and settles the first all-African final in the tournament’s history in their favour. The final at the San Martin stadium kicked off at 19:30 local time on Sunday, 01:30 GMT on Monday. Opentil’s shot took a deflection off a Moroccan defender early in the second half (amputee football is played in halves of 25 minutes), and Ghana defended the lead for the rest of the match, the Ghana Football Association said.

news.title: Infantino’s $20bn World Cup sell-off plan was to run for up to 96 years, documents show
news.lede: Management team were in line for huge payouts. Fifa denies Infantino would have profited from plan. Gianni Infantino’s failed Fifa Forward Enterprise plan could have locked football in for up to 96 years while paying its management up to 5% of the scheme’s multibillion-pound value, according to documents seen by the Guardian. Previously undisclosed communications by Fifa and Thrive Capital, the lead investor for the proposal, cast fresh light on the deal to sell off football’s crown jewels.

news.lede: Scotland Women v Sweden kicks off at 7.25pm GMT in Paisley. Find the BBC channel, live stream, squad news and date of the return leg. Scotland Women v Sweden takes place on Tuesday 1 December 2026 in the first leg of their World Cup play-off. Kick-off in Paisley is 7.25pm GMT.

news.title: FIFA Set To Approve UK Bid To Host 2035 Women’s World Cup
news.lede: FIFA is expected to approve the joint UK bid by England, Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland to host the 2035 Women’s World Cup. The United Kingdom is expected to secure the hosting rights for the 2035 FIFA Women’s World Cup, with England, Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland submitting the only joint bid for the tournament. FIFA’s 211 member associations are scheduled to decide the hosts of the 2031 and 2035 competitions on Monday, November 23, during an Extraordinary Congress to be held virtually. The proposed 2035 tournament will feature 48 national teams playing 104 matches over 39 days, making it one of the biggest editions of the women’s competition.
